chunks: And it is narrated from Jaʿfar ibn ʿUthmān, who said:

My father sent goods to al-Shām with a camel-driver, and he mentioned that one load of it was lost. So I mentioned that to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and he said, “Do you accuse him?” I said, “No.” He said, “Then do not hold him liable.”

key_terms.الشَّامِ: Syria or the region of al-Shām
key_terms.تُضَمِّنْهُ: you hold him liable for compensation

ai.seo_question: Is a camel-driver or carrier liable if entrusted goods are lost and he is not suspected?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding entrusted goods carried by a transporter. If the carrier is not suspected of wrongdoing or negligence, he is not to be held liable for the lost property.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3924 - It is narrated from Ja'far bin Uthman, who said:

My father sent some goods to Syria with a camel driver, and the camel driver claimed that one of the loads was lost. I mentioned this to Abu Abdillah (as).
Imam (as) said: "Do you suspect him?"
I said: "No."
Imam (as) said: "Then do not hold him liable."
